sections.h2: Agent, private sale or cash in Blaine
sections.html:
Blaine sellers choose among a listing agent, a buyer found on their own, and an investor who pays cash and accepts the repairs. Blaine is a large suburb, 13 miles from Minneapolis and 20 from St. Paul, so a well-kept house usually draws showings quickly. Direct sales suit houses that need repairs or carry a messy ownership history.

  • List the house and prepare for buyer financing, an appraisal and repair requests.
  • Sell it yourself, which means you handle disclosures, the deed and recording.
  • Sell for cash to an investor and skip showings and repair negotiations.

Whichever route you choose, the same Minnesota paperwork applies, and the county that records your deed is almost always Anoka County.

Population stands at 76,603, a 9.1 percent gain since April 2020 and the biggest total in Anoka County. Most of it lies in Anoka County and a piece reaches into Ramsey County. Commuters and families make up most of the buyer pool. For 2020 to 2024, 85.3 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the typical home is valued at $352,400. Monthly cost for owners with a mortgage is $2,008, median gross rent is $1,705, and median household income is $106,801. The same-house rate is 90.4 percent, so owners here tend to stay put. Test any offer against the recent sale of a comparable house in your own subdivision.

About three weeks ahead of listing, collect the documents the other side will want. Start with the tax statement, which shows your parcel number and the county that taxes it. Find the sump pump records, repair receipts and any radon test results you hold. If tenants live in the house, locate the rental license, the last inspection result and the leases.

Then draft the written disclosure. Hand it over before the purchase agreement is signed. Writing it early means you can reply the day an offer lands. If the house needs repairs you do not want to make, say so plainly in the disclosure and price accordingly. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands will still read that document, so it is the one piece of paperwork worth getting right. Sellers who skip the early gathering usually end up scrambling for permits, lease copies or repair receipts in the middle of a closing week, and that scramble is what stretches a quick sale into a slow one. A single folder, paper or digital, keeps everything in one place for the agent, the buyer and the title company.

Three districts serve Blaine, and the one tied to your address is a real selling point. Anoka-Hennepin covers most of the city, including the area from Highway 65 to University Avenue north of 99th Avenue NE. Spring Lake Park Schools covers nearly everything south of 99th Avenue NE, and Centennial Schools covers the area east of Lexington Avenue and south and east of Interstate 35W.

Lines follow streets, not neighborhoods, so neighbors a block apart may fall in separate districts. Check your address with the district before you quote one to a buyer.

sections.h2: Rental license for a Blaine rental house
sections.html:
Blaine licenses rental property every year, and a buyer who inherits your tenants takes on that duty. The license expires on December 31, and owners with three consecutive years without violations qualify for a reduced fee.

Blaine annual rental license fees

Single family, attached or detached$190
Multi-family$180 per building plus $10 per unit

Single family rentals get an interior inspection every three years and an exterior inspection every year. For a rental sale, hand the buyer the license, the last inspection result and the tenant lease documents. An owner-occupied house that you are simply selling does not need any of this.

sections.h2: Recording and closing in Anoka County
sections.html:
The county recorder accepts or rejects your deed based on a checklist. A transfer deed needs these items:

  • Deed tax of .0033 on the net consideration for prices above $3,000, set by Minnesota Statute 287.21.
  • A $5 agricultural conservation fee.
  • A completed electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value and its number on the deed.
  • A "Send tax statements to" line with the buyer's name and address.
  • Delinquent taxes paid in full before the transfer.
  • A well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or one of the two well statements the county prints for deeds.

Land records here come in two kinds, abstract and torrens, and most local parcels are abstract. A title search should therefore turn up every document tied to the lot. The title company normally files for you, but read the list so nothing surprises you.

sections.h2: Homestead status and tax bills at sale
sections.html:
Homestead tax arrives in two bills, May 15 and October 15. A statement that never came is no defense against a late fee. One point trips up many sellers: the owner must tell the assessor within 30 days if the home sells or stops being a primary residence, and the county can remove the homestead and impose penalties if no one does.

A Certificate of Real Estate Value is due at the auditor's office when a property sells, as Minnesota Statute 272.115 requires. A qualifying disabled veteran can receive a market value exclusion of up to $300,000 on homestead property, so buyers who qualify may ask about it. Have the closing agent split the current half-year between you and the buyer by closing date.

Under Minnesota Statute 513.55, you must write down any material facts you know that could adversely and significantly affect a buyer's use and enjoyment, and you must do it before signing the purchase agreement. Section 144.496 adds a radon disclosure: whether tests were done, the latest reports, any mitigation system, a radon warning statement and the Minnesota Department of Health booklet.

Blaine sits on glacial sand, ponds and wetlands, so basement moisture is a fair thing to document. Gather any sump pump records, past repairs and test results before the first showing so the written disclosure is accurate and complete.

sections.h2: After you accept a Blaine offer
sections.html: When the offer is signed, the title company reviews the land record, requests tax figures and drafts a deed that covers each checklist item. You sign the deed at closing, the delinquent-tax check clears, and the deed goes to Anoka County for recording. The Certificate of Real Estate Value follows to the auditor, and you report the sale to the assessor within 30 days if the house was your homestead. Keep copies of the signed deed, the settlement statement and the tax payoff, because they answer almost any question that comes up afterward.

faqs.q: Which county records a Blaine deed?
faqs.a: Anoka County, for nearly all of the city. A slice of Blaine is in Ramsey County, so look at the county named on your tax statement before mailing anything.

faqs.q: Who pays deed tax when I sell in Blaine?
faqs.a: The state charges .0033 of the net consideration above $3,000. Your purchase agreement decides which side covers it, so confirm with the title company.

faqs.q: Can my Blaine rental license pass to the buyer?
faqs.a: Ask Blaine Housing Services before closing. Licenses are yearly and end December 31, so expect the new owner to apply on their own and book any inspection the city wants.

faqs.q: What if my Blaine house has radon or a wet basement?
faqs.a: Put what you know in writing. State law covers known radon results and other material facts, and a seller who hides them can owe damages.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Blaine cash sale close?
faqs.a: Often within weeks, since no lender appraisal is involved. The slowest piece is usually an item missing from the recording checklist.
